notes: §1985:XI.2.4.3 SR1: 'The availability of the RECORD option of the SAME clause is dependent on the level of Sequential I-O module supported by the implementation.' WiseOwl implements the full Sequential I-O module, so the rule requires the RECORD option to be available in the Sort-Merge I-O-CONTROL paragraph: the sameClause grammar admits SAME RECORD AREA at every edition, FileControlBinder.BindIoControl screens it (ScreenSameClauses/SameOccurrenceRule) and LinkSameRecordArea makes every named file's record an implicit redefinition of one area, sort files included; no edition gate is needed. Probes at 85 (work-slice-46/c9): d/e) samerec, SAME RECORD AREA FOR an SD, a sequential FD and an indexed FD: a MOVE to the FD record is the SD record (SR VIA OR1 AAA12 SN=12), each RETURN fills the FD records (RET OR1=BBB34 XK=BBB, then AAA12), and WRITE OR1 writes it; b) sdinarea, the sort file in a plain SAME AREA clause is refused (COBOL2738), c10/d_single (one operand) is refused, c10/ok_record_only and ok_mixed compile. Witness: SAME RECORD AREA FOR SFILE OFILE shows HELLO moved to O-REC through S-REC.

next.reason: 1985: "The availability of the RECORD option of the SAME clause is dependent on the level of Sequential I-O module supported"; 2023: "No module levels; SR-12.4.6.4.3-6 lets a sort or merge file appear in a record-area format SAME clause unconditionally". 2023 drops modules and levels. The record-area SAME format is always available to sort and merge files, so the 1985 dependency on the Sequential I-O level is no longer stated.
